title: Application Round Explorer
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: Answer five questions about one college and one student, and the explorer recommends an application round, explains why, and shows its deadline, decision, and commitment dates.

learningObjectives: Students will judge which application round (ED, EA, REA, RD, or rolling) best fits a given student and college, and justify the choice using whether the round is binding and whether it allows comparing aid offers.
prerequisites: Chapter 1: The College Landscape and Application Rounds

controls: Six round checkboxes (ED, ED II, EA, REA, RD, Rolling)

keyQuestions: Why does needing to compare financial aid rule out Early Decision?
When is Regular Decision a stronger choice than any early round?
What rule do you break by applying Early Decision to two colleges?
commonMisconceptions: Applying early is always the smart move.
Early Action and Early Decision are the same thing.
assessmentOpportunities: Students justify a recommended round for a new scenario using two criteria: whether the round is binding and whether it lets the family compare aid offers.
